spots.name: White Tower of Thessaloniki
spots.summary: The White Tower of Thessaloniki is a monument and museum on the waterfront of the city of Thessaloniki, capital of the region of Macedonia in northern Greece.

spots.name: Hagia Sophia

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Hagia Sophia is a church located in Thessaloniki, Greece. With its current structure dating from the 7th century, it is one of the oldest churches in the city still standing today.

spots.name: Hagios Demetrios

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Saint Demetrius, or Hagios Demetrios, is the main sanctuary dedicated to Saint Demetrius, the patron saint of Thessaloniki, dating from a time when it was the second largest city of the Byzantine Empire.

spots.name: Rotunda

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: Started life as a Roman temple of Zeus, built by Caesar Galerius, and is almost as old as the Pantheon in Rome. The monument has a diameter of 24.5 m and its dome reaches a height of 30 m. It was converted into a Christian church during the Early Christian era, and its interior was decorated with magnificent mosaics. spots.name: Arch of Galerius and Rotunda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Arch of Galerius or Kamara (Καμάρα) and the Rotunda of Galerius (Ροτόντα) are neighbouring early fourth-century AD monuments in the city of Thessaloniki, in the region of Central Macedonia in northern Greece.

spots.name: Walls of Thessaloniki
spots.summary: The Walls of Thessaloniki are the 4 kilometer-long city walls surrounding the city of Thessaloniki during the Middle Ages and until the late 19th century, when large parts of the walls, including the entire seaward section, were demolished as part of the Ottoman authorities' restructuring of Thessaloniki's urban fabric.

spots.name: Archaeological Museum of Thessaloniki

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: The Archaeological Museum of Thessaloniki is a museum in Thessaloniki, Central Macedonia, Greece. It holds and interprets artifacts from the Prehistoric, Archaic, Classical, Hellenistic and Roman periods, mostly from the city of Thessaloniki but also from the region of Macedonia in general.

spots.name: Hamza Bey Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Hamza Bey Mosque is a former mosque in Thessaloniki, in the Central Macedonia region of Greece. Built between 1467-1468, during the Ottoman era, the mosque was abandoned in the 1820s. Modern Thessalonians commonly know it as Alkazar, after a cinema that operated in the premises for decades.

spots.name: Paleochristian and Byzantine monuments of Thessaloniki
spots.summary: The city of Thessaloniki in Macedonia, Greece, for several centuries the second-most important city of the Byzantine Empire, played an important role for Christianity during the Middle Ages and was decorated by impressive buildings.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Paleochristian and Byzantine monuments of Thessaloniki

spots.name: Church of the Acheiropoietos

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Acheiropoietos is a 5th-century Byzantine-era Greek Orthodox church, located in the city of Thessaloniki, Central Macedonia, in northern Greece. It is situated in the city's centre, at Agias Sofias street opposite Makedonomachon square.

spots.name: Aristotelous Square
spots.summary: Aristotelous Square, is the main city square of Thessaloniki, Greece, and is located on Nikis avenue, in the city center. It was designed by French architect Ernest Hébrard in 1918, but most of the square was built in the 1950s.

spots.name: OTE Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: OTE Tower is a 76-metre-tall tower located in the Thessaloniki International Exhibition Center in central Thessaloniki, Greece. The tower opened in 1970 and was renovated in 2005.

spots.name: Vlatades Monastery

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Vlatades Monastery or Vlatadon Monastery is a monastery in Ano Poli, Thessaloniki, Greece.

spots.name: Church of Saint Panteleimon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Saint Panteleimon, officially the Holy Church of Saint Panteleimon, is a Greek Orthodox church located in Thessaloniki, in the Central Macedonia region of Greece. The Byzantine-era church was built in the 14th century.

spots.name: Church of Panagia Chalkeon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Panagia Chalkeon is an 11th-century Byzantine-era Greek Orthodox church in the city of Thessaloniki, in the Central Macedonia region of northern Greece.

spots.name: Museum of Byzantine Culture
spots.summary: The Museum of Byzantine Culture is a museum in Thessaloniki, Central Macedonia, Greece, which opened in 1994.

spots.name: Heptapyrgion

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: The Heptapyrgion, modern Eptapyrgio, also popularly known by its Ottoman Turkish name Yedi Kule, is a Byzantine and Ottoman-era fortress situated on the north-eastern corner of the Acropolis of Thessaloniki in Greece.

spots.name: Church of the Holy Twelve Apostles

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Holy Apostles is a 14th-century Byzantine-era Greek Orthodox church in the city of Thessaloniki, in the Central Macedonia region of northern Greece.

spots.name: Atatürk Museum
spots.summary: Atatürk Museum is a historic house museum in Thessaloniki, Central Macedonia, Greece.

photo.author: Kemal Cenk Sarioglu from Istanbul, Turkey

spots.name: Zeitenlik
spots.summary: Zeitenlik is an Allied military cemetery and World War I memorial park in Thessaloniki, the largest military cemetery in Greece. It contains the graves of circa 20,000 Serbian, French, British, Italian, Russian and Greek soldiers and Bulgarian POWs, who died in the battles on the Salonika front during World War I.

spots.name: Modiano Market
spots.summary: Modiano Market or Stoa Modiano is an enclosed market in Thessaloniki, Greece. It was built between 1922 and 1925, after the great fire, on the site of the old Talmud Tora synagogue.

spots.name: Church of the Saviour

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Transfiguration of the Saviour is a 14th-century Byzantine chapel in Thessaloniki, Greece. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site as one of the Paleochristian and Byzantine monuments of Thessaloniki.

spots.name: New Mosque

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Yeni Mosque is a mosque in the city of Thessaloniki, northern Greece. It was built by Italian architect Vitaliano Poselli in 1902, during the Ottoman era, for the city's Dönmeh community, crypto-Jewish converts to Islam.

spots.name: Roman Forum
spots.summary: The Roman Forum of Thessaloniki is the ancient Roman-era forum of the city, located at the upper side of Aristotelous Square.

photo.author: Leandro Neumann Ciuffo from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil

spots.name: Church of St. Nicholas Orphanos

hours.note: Closed Tue, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Church of Saint Nicholas Orphanos is an early 14th-century Byzantine church in the northern Greek city of Thessaloniki.

spots.name: Bedesten of Thessaloniki

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Bedesten of Thessaloniki is a historical Ottoman market in the city of Thessaloniki, Greece, built during the reign of Sultan Mehmed II. It is located on Venizelou and Solomou streets, near the Hamza Bey Mosque and the city's old town hall.

spots.name: Alaca Imaret Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Alaca Imaret Mosque, also known as the Ishak Pasha Mosque, is a mosque in Thessaloniki, Greece. Completed in the 1480s, during the Ottoman era, the mosque was built under the direction of Ishak Pasha.

spots.name: National Theatre of Northern Greece
spots.summary: The National Theatre of Northern Greece or NTNG is an institution promoting performing arts primarily in Thessaloniki and Northern Greece, founded in 1961.

spots.name: Museum for the Macedonian Struggle

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Museum for the Macedonian Struggle is located in the centre of the city Thessaloniki in Central Macedonia, Greece. It occupies a neo-classical building designed by the renowned architect Ernst Ziller and built in 1893.

spots.name: Jewish Museum of Thessaloniki

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: The Jewish Museum of Thessaloniki is a museum in Thessaloniki, Central Macedonia, Greece. It displays the history of Sephardic Jews and Jewish life in Thessaloniki. The museum is being run by the Jewish community of the city.

spots.summary: The Church of Prophet Elijah is a 14th-century Byzantine-era Greek Orthodox church in the Ano Poli neighbourhood of the city of Thessaloniki, in the Central Macedonia region of northern Greece.

spots.summary: Bey Hamam, alternatively known as the "Baths of Paradise", is a Turkish bathhouse located along Egnatia Street in Thessaloniki, east of Panagia Chalkeon.

spots.name: Eleftherias Square
spots.summary: Eleftherias Square is a central square in downtown Thessaloniki, Greece. It takes its name from the Young Turk Revolution, which began in the square in 1908.

spots.summary: The Church of Hosios David is a late 5th-century church in Thessaloniki, in the Central Macedonia region of Greece. During Byzantine times, it functioned as the katholikon of the Latomos Monastery, and was adorned with rich mosaic and fresco decoration, which was renewed in the 12th–14th centuries.

spots.summary: The Byzantine Bath of the Upper City in Thessaloniki is one of the few and best preserved of the Byzantine baths that have survived from the Byzantine period in Greece. It is located on the Theotokopoulou Street in the Upper Old Town of Thessaloniki.

spots.name: Egnatia Street
spots.summary: Egnatia Street is the main commercial street in downtown Thessaloniki. The road is named for the Roman-era Via Egnatia which passed near the city.

spots.name: Government House
spots.summary: The Konak, otherwise known as the Government House, is an Ottoman-era building in central Thessaloniki, Greece. Originally built in 1891 as the residence (konak) of the governor-general (veli) of the Salonica Vilayet and the seat of the Ottoman authorities, it now houses the Ministry of Macedonia and Thrace.

spots.name: Yahudi Hamam
spots.summary: The Yahudi Hamam is an Ottoman-era bath in Thessaloniki, Greece. Located at the intersection of Vasileos Irakleiou and Frangini streets, the bath dates to the 16th century. Its name means "Bath of the Jews", as the area was predominantly settled by Sephardi Jews.

spots.summary: Nikis Avenue is the central waterfront avenue in Thessaloniki, Greece. The three lane eastward avenue stretches from Eleftherias Square in the west, in front of Aristotelous Square to the White Tower in the east, where it meets with Alexander the Great Avenue.

spots.summary: Mikro Emvolo, also called Karabournaki (Καραμπουρνάκι), is the cape of Kalamaria in northeastern Thessaloniki and a district of the local municipality. Its name comes from kara burun in Turkish, meaning 'black peninsula'. + Greek -aki (diminutive).

spots.summary: Nice place with good vegan food. This is the best place to enjoy vegan mezze in Thessaloniki. You can find a decently sized menu with several options to choose from. The space is very alternative but small with some outdoor seating and expect to have to wait for seating if you arrive at peak hours. The beet salad is fresh and delicious.
